title: Red lentil and carrot puree
summary: Red lentils cook down to a creamy puree in 15 minutes and bring plenty of iron and protein to a first bowl.
texture: Smooth and creamy. Red lentils break down completely, so blending gives a velvety texture. Thin as needed.
ingredients: Breast milk, prepared infant formula or water, to thin
steps: Put the lentils, carrot and water in a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, for 15 to 20 minutes, until the lentils are mushy and the carrot is very soft. Add a splash of water if it gets dry.
Blend until smooth, thinning to a spoonable texture.
Cool to lukewarm and check the temperature before serving.
choking: Blend until there are no firm carrot pieces.
Pick over the dry lentils for tiny stones before rinsing.
storage: Fridge up to 2 days in a sealed container, or freeze in an ice-cube tray, then bag the cubes, up to 1 month. Thaw in the fridge and warm gently. Stir and check the temperature before serving.
tips: Serve with a vitamin C food, like a spoonful of mashed strawberry or pureed broccoli, to help baby absorb the iron.
Lentils can make some babies gassy at first. Start with a few spoonfuls.
